DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 60 s. 2022 June 30, 2022 MR. ALI SMITH PAJOTA alipajotal 10994@gmaiI.com Dear Mr. Pajota: This has reference to your e-mail dated June 7, 2022 addressed to the Presidential Complaint Center (PCC) requesting clarification on whether an incumbent Mayor who ran for the position of Governor can still sign government documents even during the election ban. We answer in the affirmative. An elective official, including an incumbent Mayor, can generally sign government documents, except those connected with the prohibition brought about by the election ban enforced by the Commission on Elections such as the use of government funds in election campaigns and rallies or even on disguised local government activities but tend to support an electoral candidate is an election offense proscribed under Section 261 (o), Title XXII, of the Omnibus Election Code, viz: "Section 261 Prohibited Acts: xxx o. Use of public funds, money deposited in trust, equipment, facilities owned or controlled by the govemment for an election campaign. Any person who uses under any guise whatsoever, directly or indirectly, (1) public funds or money deposited with, or held in trust by, public financing institutions or by. govemment offices, banks, or agencies; (2) any printing press, radio, or television station or audio-visual equipment operated by the Govemment or by its divisions, sub-divisions, agencies or instrumentalities, including govemment-owned or controlled corporations, or by the Armed Forces of the Philippines; or (3) any equipment, vehicle, facility, apparatus, or paraphernalia owned by the government or by its political subdivisions, agencies including govemment-owned or controlled corporations, or by the Armed Forces of the Philippines for any election campaign or for any partisan political activity. " In addition, there is COMELEC Resolution No. 10747, RULES AND REGULATIONS ON PROHIBITION AGAINST RELEASE, DISBURSEMNET OF PUBLIC FUNDS AND CONSTRUCTION OF PUBLIC WORKS, AND ISSUANCE OF TREASURY WARRANTS AND SIMILAR DEVICES (SECTION 261 (V), (W) OF THE OMNIBUS "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

ELECTION CODE) IN CONNECTION WITH MAY 9, 2022 SYNCHRONIZED NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS. Considering, however, of the passing of the 2022 Presidential and Local Elections and the termination of the period of prohibition provided by Section 2 of COMELEC Resolution No. 10747, the foregoing discussion is respectfully presented for academic purposes and for any guidance it may serve. On a final note, it may be relevant to stress that the term of office of municipal, city and provincial elective officials shall end at noon on June 30, 2022. Until such time, the aforesaid elective officials are still authorized to discharge their functions appurtenant to their respective offices. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: I INGAN Unders etary for Local Government OUSLG/MLI/LLLS-LRA L 1k . /clp Copy furnished: PRE IDENTIAL COMPLAINT CENTER Office of the President J.P.
